item.title: Oregon Receives More Bad News on Dante Moore Ahead of Illinois Showdown
item.description: An ambulance took Dante Moore off the field at the Los Angeles Memorial Coliseum on Sept. 26, more than 10 minutes after a hit from a USC linebacker left him on his back during Oregon’s 41-27 win. The Ducks have played twice since without their starting quarterback, falling 17-15 to a UCLA team that is now 6-0 and rallying past Nebraska 17-14. Moore will miss a third straight game Saturday at Illinois after the Big Ten’s availability report listed him as out Wednesday night, along with leading receiver Evan Stewart. Dan Lanning has said several times that Moore is practicing and throwing, and Moore was spotted throwing passes before each of the last two games without dressing for either. Lanning has declined to give a timeline for his return or say if Moore has cleared concussion protocol. Oregon quarterback Dante Moore walks off the field as the Oregon Ducks face the Indiana Hoosiers in the Peach Bowl on Jan. 9, 2026, at Mercedes-Benz Stadium in Atlanta, Georgia. “I’m not able to tell you that,” Lanning said on Monday when asked about Moore’s medical status. That answer leaves the Ducks preparing for a road game with the quarterback job still unsettled, after the position changed hands inside each of the last two games. Oregon QB Dante Moore has been ruled OUT for Saturday’s game vs. Illinois. Moore will miss his third straight game as he continues to recover from a concussion. That tough hit has cost Moore a lot of games — NFL Rumors (@nflrums) October 22, 2026 What Oregon’s offense has looked like without Moore Dylan Raiola replaced Moore at USC and threw for 289 yards in relief. He started against UCLA and gave way to third-string quarterback Brock Thomas in the loss. A week later, Thomas got the start against Nebraska, and Raiola came back in during the fourth quarter to throw the game-winning touchdown. Oregon scored at least 31 points in each of its first four games, a run that included 84 against FCS opponent Portland State. The 15 points against UCLA and 17 against Nebraska are the Ducks’ two lowest totals of the season, and both came with Moore watching from the sideline. Stewart, who has team highs of 27 catches, 352 yards and four touchdowns, will miss a second straight game. Oregon lists him out with an undisclosed injury after he was arrested early Sunday in Springfield, Oregon, on a charge of driving under the influence of intoxicants. Oregon quarterback Dante Moore walks the field after the Ducks’ loss as the Oregon Ducks face the Indiana Hoosiers in the Peach Bowl on Jan. 9, 2026, at Mercedes-Benz Stadium in Atlanta, Georgia. Tight end Jamari Johnson, who was cited for speeding in the Springfield area early that same Sunday, was not on the availability report. He has 17 catches for 224 yards and two touchdowns this season and is in line to play Saturday. Lanning has not named a starter for Illinois. He started against UCLA and gave way to third-string quarterback Brock Thomas in the loss. item.title: Vincent Kompany urges patience over Lennart Karl as Bayern Munich boss backs teenager to rediscover best form
item.description: Bayern Munich head coach Vincent Kompany has called for calm regarding the recent form of teenage attacker Lennart Karl after leaving the youngster on the bench against Arsenal. Despite a reduction in playing time at the Allianz Arena, the Belgian tactician insists the highly-rated forward retains the full backing of his staff. Belgian tactician defends benched youngster Kompany remains completely unconcerned by Karl's slow start to the campaign and is confident the 18-year-old forward will soon return to peak form. Following an eye-catching breakthrough season, the teenager has seen his minutes restricted in recent weeks. Notably, he was named among the substitutes for Wednesday's 2-2 Champions League draw with Arsenal despite winger Michael Olise missing out through suspension. Coaching staff maintain complete faith imago-sport-1084861689.jpg Karl established himself as one of Bavaria's brightest prospects last term courtesy of his technical quality, direct dribbling and clinical finishing in the final third. However, he is still working to rebuild his match sharpness after a serious muscle injury suffered in June ruled him out of the 2026 World Cup and kept him sidelined for approximately 12 weeks until late August. Addressing the youngster's reduced role after the final whistle against Arsenal, Kompany explained: "The rhythm and performances will come. He's not performing at the level he had last season, but that's also okay. He knows that it happens, he knows we're patient with him. At some point his moment will come and he will show us the Lennart Karl that we all know." Summer setback stalls upward trajectory Returning from a three-month layoff has proven doubly challenging for the academy graduate due to the fierce competition for attacking places at the club. Even when Olise was unavailable in midweek, the German champions could call upon established forwards such as Luis Diaz, Serge Gnabry and Jamal Musiala, while summer signing Ismail Saibari has added further depth to the frontline. Highlighting the physical hurdles the teenager has had to overcome since the summer, the Bayern boss added: "He's still young, he had a few injuries. It will come, I'm not worried." Fierce competition awaits returning prospect imago-sport-1084858035.jpg Rather than rushing the youngster back into the starting lineup, Bayern's coaching staff are prepared to give him time to rebuild his confidence and rhythm gradually. Karl's immediate focus will be making an impact off the bench during upcoming Bundesliga and Champions League fixtures to force his way past his senior team-mates. With club chiefs keeping faith in his ability, the forward has a clear platform to revive his season.

item.title: Lakers predicted to trade for Mavericks' $88M perfect Luka Doncic lob threat with Finals experience
item.description: Lakers predicted to trade for Mavericks' $88M perfect Luka Doncic lob threat with Finals experience originally appeared on The Sporting News . Add The Sporting News as a Preferred Source by clicking here . The Los Angeles Lakers made the right decision by paying up for Walker Kessler this summer, and that move showed its value on Wednesday night. However, the team still has a significant drop-off at center when Kevon Looney checks into the game. LA still needs to add another center to the mix, and the Lakers have been searching for one for some time. “The Lakers are still monitoring the market for big men, team sources told The Athletic," The Athletic's Dan Woike reported. "They traded for Walker Kessler and signed Kevon Looney to play center, and Mamukelashvili can play the position, too. The team could address the position either by trade or signing, like with potentially adding Thybulle. The roster is currently at full capacity." Just last week, Los Angeles tried to make a deal for another center by reaching out about Jericho Sims. “League sources say that the Lakers and Bucks have held exploratory trade discussions on a framework that would ship former first-round selection Dalton Knecht to Milwaukee (along with second-round draft capital) in exchange for big man Jericho Sims," Jake Fischer wrote on the Stein Line. "Yet it must be said that I've also heard some pessimism from sources briefed on those talks that such a trade will actually go through." Bleacher Report's Dan Favale believes the Lakers should pursue a trade for Dallas Mavericks forward PJ Washington. “PJ Washington comes close to meeting that criterion. He fits like a glove next to Walker Kessler at the 5 when his three-ball is falling, and though he's not a defender who turns the water off, he can be moved up and down the matchup ladder. Head coach JJ Redick can even use him for backup-center tick when Kessler is catching a breather,” Favale wrote. Washington may not be the biggest big man in the league, but he brings plenty of athleticism and versatility to the frontcourt. He also reached the NBA Finals alongside Luka Doncic with the Mavericks, giving him experience playing alongside the Lakers star. Washington is currently on an $88 million contract with Dallas. Adding the versatile forward would give Los Angeles another valuable frontcourt option and make an already athletic roster even more dynamic. item.title: 📵 Smartphones out of stadiums? Bundesliga club introduces wild new rule
item.description: 📵 Smartphones out of stadiums? Bundesliga club introduces wild new rule Whether at concerts, shows or football stadiums, smartphones are becoming a nuisance at more and more live events. In stadiums, too, you always see plenty of people taking photos or tapping away on their phones instead of properly watching the match and soaking up the atmosphere. Of course, that’s everyone’s own choice—but one Bundesliga club now wants to give fans an incentive to spend less time fiddling with their phones during their stadium visit. Borussia Dortmund is introducing a new rewards system: the official BVB app now features a new Fan Mode. During home matches, the app tracks how long the smartphone’s screen stays locked. Users earn points for every minute they spend without actively using their phones. BVB is therefore taking a new approach to engaging with fans, aiming to shift attention in the stadium back towards the match. Fans can use their phones again at half-time without losing any points. The results are tallied after the final whistle, and the top participants can win prizes, such as BVB shirts or fan shop vouchers. The optional Fan Mode is set to be available for the first time during Saturday evening’s big match against Eintracht Frankfurt. At the launch of the initiative, which the club developed with a partner, BVB managing director Carsten Cramer spoke about the importance of shared stadium experiences: “Over 81,000 people in the stadium, singing, holding their breath and cheering together: that sense of being here, right now, is irreplaceable. And that’s exactly what we’re putting centre stage together,” said Cramer. What do you think of this unusual new stadium initiative? A good way to tackle annoying phone use during matches, or a bit over the top? Let us know in the comments! This article was translated into English by Artificial Intelligence. You can read the original version in 🇩🇪 here.

item.title: David Benavidez’s next fight confirmed as Jai Opetaia wait goes on
item.description: David Benavidez will do battle with Michael Cieslak in a three-belt unification bout, leaving Zuffa Boxing champion Jai Opetaia to wait for his desired cruiserweight clash with the undefeated American. Benavidez (32-0, 26 KOs) comes off his knockout win over Gilberto Ramirez in May, which saw the 29-year-old get the finish in round six after dominating to that point. He will now put his WBO and WBA world cruiserweight titles on the line against WBC champion Cieslak (28-2, 22 KOs) on 5 December, who stopped Jean Pascal last June to win the vacant belt. Cieslak’s last loss came four years ago to Briton Lawrence Okolie, who edged him on the scorecards in a bout at the O2 Arena. While fighting Cieslak gives Benavidez the chance to go one step closer to undisputed champion status, it means fans will have to hold out for a fight with Australian superstar Opetaia. The pair stoked the fire last month when Benavidez faced off with Opetaia following his win over Norair Mikaeljan at a Zuffa event in Las Vegas, accepting his callout in the ring. “This is a great fighter, we’re going to give the fans a great fight,” Benavidez said. “I like this man, it looks like he likes war, I’m the exact same way so we’re going to give the fans a hell of a fight.” Opetaia had previously suggested Benavidez’s demands were holding up the fight getting booked, saying he wanted to fight on Mexican holiday Cinco de Mayo, with the undefeated Australia insisting he was not giving “any pushback”. “Just call me and I'll be there. Just give me the date and I'll be there,” he said before the Mikaeljan fight. Jai Opetaia called out David Benavidez last month (Getty) Their in-ring exchange seemed to show a fight was teetering on confirmation but Benavidez will instead turn his attention to Cieslak this winter. Benavidez still plans to fight Opetaia after the Cieslak clash, which would be one of a trio of blockbuster bouts he hopes to land as part of a new deal. "I'm going to sign a three-fight contract," said Benavidez. "After this fight, we're talking about [Jai] Opetaia, we're talking about [Artur] Beterbiev, and we are maybe talking about [Oleksandr] Usyk. "So those fights are going to be at cruiserweight, and I'm a little bit confused about the one with Usyk. That might either be at cruiserweight or heavyweight. “Those are three great fights that need to happen, and they are going to happen. I'm not just here saying I'm going to fight these guys and then I never fight them. I'm going to fight these guys because this is who I want to fight. "I want Opetaia, I want Beterbiev and I want Usyk."

item.title: ‘Why Are You So Eager to Get Sean McVay?’ ‘I Don’t Get It’ — Boston Announcer Questions Hype Around Hiring Rams HC for Amazon’s NFL Booth
item.description: ‘Why Are You So Eager to Get Sean McVay?’ ‘I Don’t Get It’ — Boston Announcer Questions Hype Around Hiring Rams HC for Amazon’s NFL Booth Sean McVay has been linked to a potential move to the broadcast booth for years, but not everyone understands Amazon’s eagerness to land the Los Angeles Rams coach. Following Andrew Marchand’s report in The Athletic on Kirk Herbstreit’s new Prime Video deal, which reportedly gives the network flexibility to pursue McVay, Boston College announcer Jon Meterparel questioned why the company is so determined to bring him into its Thursday Night Football booth. Amazon’s Interest in Sean McVay Goes Back to 2022 When Marchand reported last month that Prime Video had extended Herbstreit as its TNF analyst, the deal came with a catch. It leaves Amazon room to move on if one of its preferred candidates becomes available, most notably pointing to McVay. However, Marchand’s own podcast co-host doesn’t buy the idea. “I don’t understand why there’s such a rush to get Sean McVay in a booth,” Meterparel said. Marchand’s report also put the extension at multiple seasons and more than $10 million a year. That’s shorter than the five-year contract Herbstreit first signed with Prime Video. Prime Video has eyed McVay since the start of its TNF era. Weeks after his Rams won Super Bowl 56 in February 2022, he was set to meet with Prime Video about the analyst job, and Marchand reported at the time that Amazon was willing to pay up to $100 million over five years. SET YOUR LINEUPS: PFN’s Free Fantasy Start/Sit Optimizer McVay stayed put, and Amazon then signed Herbstreit to pair with Al Michaels. But does a winning coach make a winning analyst? Meterparel’s case was exactly about that, using a few famous examples. “There was a rush to get Bill Walsh in a booth. He stunk. There was a rush to get Bill Parcells in a booth. He stunk. Not that McVay’s a Walsh or Parcells at this point in his career. Belichick, okay, nothing great. I don’t know if it’s a guarantee. If I’m Amazon, why are you so eager to get Sean McVay? I don’t get it.” Meterparel listed traits in McVay that could work in his favor in connecting with a young audience. However, he isn’t convinced that is enough to enjoy success in the booth. “I know he’s a good-looking dude. I know he has kind of the California lifestyle going on. I know he’ll fit in maybe nicely with a younger crowd. I just don’t get it.” On Monday’s episode of his podcast, Marchand explained how Amazon’s flexibility works: “I think it’s a three-year deal; I didn’t write that originally. There are outs after Year 1 and 2. So I think Kirk would get his full money if it happened after this year. It’s basically buyouts.” So why would Herbstreit sign a deal that leaves the door open for someone else? “Why not? Marchand came back to the same target: “McVay is one thing. I don’t think Amazon Prime Video would go after Troy Aikman. I think they want Sean McVay.” Herbstreit opened this season in the last year of his contract, as did two other marquee NFL analysts, ESPN’s Aikman and Fox’s Greg Olsen. The Amazon extension made him the first of the three to sign a new NFL deal. His college future isn’t settled, though. The ESPN deal that keeps him on the “College GameDay” set and in the network’s top college booth expires after this season too, and Marchand has reported that ESPN won’t address it until the college season ends. Amazon has kept the play-by-play chair flexible as well. Michaels, 81, has worked on one-year deals since his original three-year contract ran out. McVay, meanwhile, is still the Rams’ head coach, with the team currently 2-4 after six weeks. Los Angeles currently has a 10.4% chance of making the playoffs and has seen its Super Bowl-winning odds drop to 0.1% per PFN’s Football Playoff Meter . The next headset McVay puts on will be on the sideline on Sunday, when the Rams visit the Las Vegas Raiders. This article originally appeared on Pro Football Network .

item.title: Tottenham finally have lift-off, but Chelsea could quickly spoil the party
item.description: Tottenham finally have lift-off, but Chelsea could quickly spoil the party Tottenham Hotspur finally have something to build on after securing their first Premier League victory of the season, but Saturday’s London derby against Chelsea will reveal how much progress they have made. Roberto De Zerbi’s side ended their six-match winless start with a 3-1 victory over Coventry City on Monday, offering supporters a rare reason for optimism. Goals from James Maddison, Omar Marmoush and Ben Davies provided a welcome attacking improvement for a team that has struggled throughout 2026. However, facing Chelsea at Stamford Bridge represents a considerably tougher examination of Tottenham’s emerging confidence. The Blues have rediscovered their attacking rhythm under Xabi Alonso, scoring seven goals across consecutive league victories over Bournemouth and Everton. Their 5-1 demolition of Bournemouth demonstrated their attacking potential, while the subsequent 2-0 victory at Everton suggested improvements defensively. Chelsea have scored 17 goals in seven league matches and climbed into the top four, strengthening their ambitions of challenging the division’s leading clubs. For Tottenham, disrupting that momentum would represent an important statement in De Zerbi’s attempt to establish a new identity. The Italian’s attacking philosophy offers the possibility of an entertaining contest, but his players must avoid leaving excessive space for Chelsea’s dangerous forwards. Cole Palmer, Joao Pedro and Morgan Rogers possess the creativity and movement to punish defensive mistakes, particularly when opponents commit numbers forward. Chelsea also have recent history firmly on their side, having won six consecutive Premier League meetings with Tottenham. Spurs have managed just one victory in their last 36 league visits to Stamford Bridge, highlighting the scale of Saturday’s challenge. Nevertheless, their breakthrough against Coventry could provide the psychological lift required to approach this fixture with greater belief. Maddison’s return to goalscoring form is particularly encouraging, while Dejan Kulusevski’s availability offers another potential source of creativity. Tottenham must also overcome several injury concerns, making De Zerbi’s selection decisions especially important. Chelsea have their own problems, including the absence of goalkeeper Emiliano Martinez, whose injury could offer Spurs opportunities to test an inexperienced replacement. However, Tottenham cannot rely on Chelsea’s vulnerabilities without demonstrating greater consistency in possession and defensive organisation. Their victory over Coventry was a necessary first step, but competing with an in-form Chelsea side would provide stronger evidence of genuine improvement. The hosts remain favourites given their attacking quality, confidence and formidable record in this fixture. item.title: Spalletti does not understand why Juventus winner was disallowed
item.description: Spalletti does not understand why Juventus winner was disallowed Luciano Spalletti has questioned the interpretation of the rule that led to Jhon Lucumi’s goal against Rennes being disallowed, after Juventus initially celebrated what they believed was a late winner. The defender thought he had secured a deserved victory for the Bianconeri, who appeared to have scored a decisive goal late in the match. Juventus had enjoyed late success in their previous European fixture, and the prospect of another dramatic finish raised hopes among the players and supporters. However, Lucumi’s celebrations were short-lived, as he appeared to be in an offside position when the ball was played. Following a review, the goal was disallowed, forcing Juventus to settle for a draw instead of claiming victory. UEFA uses advanced technology to assess offside decisions, and the available replays appeared to show that the Juventus defender was in an offside position when he scored. Nevertheless, Spalletti questioned whether the decision was justified, particularly given his belief that Lucumi had not interfered with the Rennes defender. Spalletti questions the VAR decision The Juventus manager was left frustrated by the ruling and admitted that he wanted to investigate the interpretation of the law further. Although he acknowledged the referee’s overall performance, he expressed disappointment with the decision that denied his team a potential winner. Speaking after the match, Spalletti explained his reaction to the incident. As quoted by Football Italia , he said: “I didn’t understand it, and I’m going to look into it. “When I saw it in the dressing room, I was surprised and disappointed. The Rennes player could have cleared that ball and Lucumí didn’t impede him. I thought I knew this rule, but after tonight I have a lot of doubts. The referee was very good, but a little less good on this incident.” Juventus must take their chances earlier The disallowed goal will leave Juventus reflecting on an opportunity to secure three points. However, the incident also highlights the importance of creating and converting chances throughout a match rather than relying on late goals to decide the outcome. The Bianconeri must now focus on their next fixture and aim to produce more consistent attacking performances. Scoring earlier and making better use of their opportunities would help reduce the pressure of chasing results in the closing stages.

Spalletti questions the VAR decision The Juventus manager was left frustrated by the ruling and admitted that he wanted to investigate the interpretation of the law further. Although he acknowledged the referee’s overall performance, he expressed disappointment with the decision that denied his team a potential winner. Speaking after the match, Spalletti explained his reaction to the incident. As quoted by Football Italia , he said: “I didn’t understand it, and I’m going to look into it. “When I saw it in the dressing room, I was surprised and disappointed. The Rennes player could have cleared that ball and Lucumí didn’t impede him. I thought I knew this rule, but after tonight I have a lot of doubts. The referee was very good, but a little less good on this incident.” Juventus must take their chances earlier The disallowed goal will leave Juventus reflecting on an opportunity to secure three points. However, the incident also highlights the importance of creating and converting chances throughout a match rather than relying on late goals to decide the outcome. The Bianconeri must now focus on their next fixture and aim to produce more consistent attacking performances. Scoring earlier and making better use of their opportunities would help reduce the pressure of chasing results in the closing stages.

item.title: Harry Kane admits Arsenal ‘punished’ Bayern Munich
item.description: Harry Kane admits Arsenal ‘punished’ Bayern Munich Harry Kane has admitted that Arsenal ‘punished’ Bayern Munich for failing to kill the game off in midweek, adding that a draw was probably a fair result. Photo by Alex Grimm/Getty Images Former Tottenham Hotspur striker Harry Kane thought he’d earned Bayern Munich three points in their Champions League clash with Arsenal in midweek, having given the team the lead with yet another penalty against the Gunners. Bayern had the chance to kill the match with one particularly dangerous counter attack, but Arsenal managed to withstand it, and the Gunners then began to dominate the game. Speaking after the game, Kane admitted Bayern were punished by a good Arsenal team for failing to finish things off, adding that a draw was a fair result in the end. Photo by Alex Grimm/Getty Images “We looked dangerous, we got the goal and we had a moment to kill the game off,” Kane said . “We had the momentum, they looked tired, but then we got caught in a low block for final 15 minutes and they punished us with the goal. “The draw was probably a fair result overall. I think we could have been a bit more clinical in the final third. But there are a lot of games, we’ve got a lot of players with injuries who are missing tonight. In the end, we’ll take the point and move on. “As the game got a little stretched towards the end, they grew into it and they’re a good physical team.” Photo by Leonhard Simon/Getty Images Getting a draw away to your Pot 1 opponent is certainly an encouraging sign, especially when the performance was strong enough to deserve it. Arsenal could even have won the game, with Bayern getting a big slice of luck with their penalty (deflected into Kane’s path and then powered onto Jurrien Timber’s arm in a natural position), and requiring a top save from Manuel Neuer to stop Bruno Guimaraes scoring a header. The Gunners still need to play their other Pot 1 team, Real Madrid, at the Emirates Stadium. But after getting a good draw away to Bayern, they’ll feel confident of a result against any opponent. Photo by Alex Grimm/Getty Images

item.title: Mumbai vice-captain Ayush Mhatre undergoes surgery for Grade 4 hamstring tear, faces four-month layoff
item.description: MUMBAI: Mumbai's opener and newly-appointed vice-captain Ayush Mhatre, who suffered from a recurrence of his right hamstring (Grade 4 tear) injury recently, underwent surgery on Thursday at the at the Kokilaben Dhirubhai Ambani Hospital here, with India's sports orthopedic Mumbai-based surgeon Dr Dinshaw Pardiwala doing the job, TOI has learnt. "Ayush underwent a 90-minute surgery for 'Hamstring Grade 4 tear repair,' for a recurrent injury on right hamstring. He was operated upon by Dr Dinshaw Pardiwala. He is comfortable and walking. He will be discharged today evening," a source tracking developments told this paper on Friday. "He will be out of action for four months," the source added. It means that the 19-year-old batter is unlikely to play for Mumbai the remainder of the 2026-27 season. Pardiwala has has helped some of the biggest names in in Team India (he has operated upon Rishabh Pant, Jasprit Bumrah, Ravindra Jadeja and many other top cricketers) and Olympic sports (Olympic medal winners Neeraj Chopra, Vinesh Phogat, PV Sindhu) to overcome injuries and return to match fitness. The 19-year-old batter’s right hamstring injury recurred during Mumbai's innings and 155 run win over Chandigarh at the Wankhede Stadium in their opening match of the 2026-27 Ranji Trophy season. Mhatre suffered the injury while taking a run on Day One during his 48-run knock in the first innings. The talented teenaged batter underwent rehabilitation for injuries to both his left and right hamstring for almost three months at the BCCI’s Centre of Excellence in Bengaluru, after being ruled out of action due to the injury from the second half of IPL-2027 while playing for the Chennai Super Kings. The injury is a big setback for Mhatre, who had just been named as Siddhesh Lad's deputy for the Ranji Trophy by the Mumbai selectors. The top-order batter had previously suffered a left hamstring injury while playing for Chennai Super Kings, which ruled him out of action for almost the last five months, and forced him to miss the T20 Mumbai tournament in June, the India A tour to Sri Lanka, followed by the Duleep Trophy in Aug. He then suffered a right hamstring injury too, which delayed his comeback. When he first suffered the injury on April 18, during CSK’s match against Sunrisers Hyderabad, Mhatre was CSK’s leading run-scorer in the tournament with 201 runs in six innings at a strike rate of 177.87. 135139391

item.title: Heat predicted to trade for $134M 2-time NBA champion, All-Star to pair with Giannis Antetokounmpo
item.description: Heat predicted to trade for $134M 2-time NBA champion, All-Star to pair with Giannis Antetokounmpo originally appeared on The Sporting News . Add The Sporting News as a Preferred Source by clicking here . The Miami Heat are off and running after opening their regular season against the Minnesota Timberwolves on Wednesday night. However, the game didn't go the way they wanted, despite a major offseason that raised expectations. This offseason was a huge one for Miami as the team went all in on winning a championship. The first major move was trading for Giannis Antetokounmpo. “The Milwaukee Bucks are trading franchise icon Giannis Antetokounmpo and Bobby Portis to the Miami Heat for Tyler Herro, Kel'el Ware, Jaime Jaquez Jr., Kasparas Jakucionis, three first-round picks (including No. 13 in Tuesday's NBA draft), one pick swap and one second-round pick, sources told ESPN. The Heat are sending to Milwaukee unprotected first-rounders in 2031 and 2033 along with No. 13, a pick swap in 2030 and a 2033 second-rounder, according to sources," ESPN's Shams Charania wrote. In free agency, the team added veterans Klay Thompson and Tim Hardaway Jr. Still, Miami could make another move to strengthen its roster. CBS Sports' Sam Quinn believes the Heat could trade for veteran guard Jrue Holiday. “The Blazers have too many guards and they'll need to create cap space to renegotiate-and-extend Deni Avdija next offseason if they want to keep him out of 2028 free agency. One of these guards is getting traded, and if the Blazers really do wind up starting Damian Lillard and Ja Morant together, bringing Holiday off the bench at this salary seems a tad wasteful, especially if they plan to keep budding defensive ace Scoot Henderson next summer. Anywhere. There is not a team in the history of basketball that would not be improved by Jrue Holiday's presence. Low-maintenance offense, still strong defense and an all-time teammate. Take your pick on who can fit the salary. The usual suspects (Detroit, Toronto, Miami),” Quinn wrote. Acquiring Holiday would be a significant move for Miami and could make the team even more dangerous. Davion Mitchell is currently the starting point guard, but adding Holiday could allow the Heat to use Mitchell's explosiveness off the bench. The move would also reunite Holiday and Antetokounmpo, who won an NBA championship together with the Milwaukee Bucks. Holiday is currently playing on a $134 million contract with the Portland Trail Blazers . The Heat have made it clear that they are focused on winning a championship, and adding a veteran like Holiday would be another major move toward that goal. More NBA news: Warriors' Yaxel Lendeborg reveals why he got a technical during exchange with Lakers' Luka Doncic Mavericks sign former first-rounder, ex-Grizzlies and Jazz combo-guard after waiving Dwight Powell Warriors attempting to trade Kristaps Porzingis for $108M rim protector with Finals experience Lakers' Luka Doncic makes strong promise to LA

item.title: Hoffenheim coach says that UEFA fixtures list is 'madness'
item.description: Hoffenheim coach Christian Ilzer gestures on the touchline during the UEFA Europa League soccer match between TSG 1899 Hoffenheim and Olympique Lyon at SNP Arena. (is associated with: «Hoffenheim coach says that UEFA fixtures list is 'madness'») Uwe Anspach/dpa Hoffenheim coach Christian Ilzer has hit out at European governing body UEFA over player workload, especially in connection with national team duties. "The UEFA fixtures list is madness," Ilzer said after his team's 3-0 victory over Olympique Lyon on Thursday in the Europa League. Looking at the latest injuries in the Champions League from clubs including Paris Saint-Germain, Bayern Munich and Barcelona, he suggested that UEFA "may consider statistics on this as well." PSG lost Ousmane Dembélé and Marquinhos on muscle injuries and Khvicha Kvaratskhelia on a ruptured cruciate knee ligament. Barcelona's Dani Olmo and Bayern's Luis Díaz are also sidelined with muscular problems. Ilzer said that club coaches are trying to manage the players' workload, which, however, is almost impossible because they are questioned as soon as "you rotate a top player out of the team." His biggest criticism concerned the national team calendar including the Nations League, with Kicker sports magazine saying that 18 Hoffenheim players were on international duty during the last window with four matches per team. “The focus of the national teams should be on the European Championship and the World Cup. These are the major highlights for the players, they are the major highlights for all national associations. That is what we should be working towards, and that is what we must qualify for," he said. "We don’t need an artificial Nations League. In my opinion, a Nations League is simply too much for the fixture list to cope with," he said, calling for a thorough review.

item.title: Kinnelon volleyball players return to celebrate program's anniversary
item.description: KINNELON — Kara (Crampton) Woodruff didn't think she'd be a volleyball player. Lacrosse was her main sport, and she'd already been talked into trying out for indoor track and field before her freshman year at Kinnelon High School even started. But a chance meeting with Colts volleyball coach Stephanie Manco changed things. Woodruff's cousin, Krystina (Mongelli) McHugh, had been part of the original Kinnelon volleyball team when it launched in 2001. She knew Manco since middle-school softball clinics. Manco's daughter, Madison, was the flower girl in McHugh's wedding. So when Manco asked Woodruff to join the freshman team, there was no question what the answer should be. Both Woodruf and McHugh were part of a group of Kinnelon alumni and families who turned up to celebrate the volleyball team's 25th anniversary on Oct. 22. The Colts defeated Hanover Park, 25-11, 25-15, in their Senior Night match. "When we started this, we knew nothing about volleyball, except playing in gym class," said McHugh, whose 11-year-old daughter Kyleigh is about to start middle-school volleyball in Pequannock – along with soccer, basketball and lacrosse. "Coming here and seeing how skilled they are, it's amazing we were part of it. They look very very good. They obviously had excellent coaching," McHugh said. Flashback! Kinnelon girls volleyball takes down Bogota to win first sectional title since 2019 Growing Kinnelon volleyball Going straight to varsity in their debut season, the Colts finished well under .500, but, Manco said, "We understood what we had to do to get the program going." Kinnelon was able to add JV a year later, and then a freshman team. Initially, Stephanie Finke , who won three straight NJSIAA titles as Paramus Catholic's middle hitter, became the middle-school coach under Manco. When Manco stepped down after the 2009 season to spend more time with Madison and her twin sons, who were all under 4 years old, Finke got the top varsity job. Manco didn't stay away for long, coming back two years later as Finke's freshman coach. Both now coach the middle-school program together, with 50 or 60 girls for six weeks snuggled between basketball and spring sports. Finke works on the offense, and Manco the defense. Milestone! Kinnelon volleyball sweeps doubleheader to give head coach Stephanie Finke 200th career win The Colts won three consecutive Northern Hills Conference titles from 2003 to 2005 – just two years after they were founded – and now have 10 division titles. They won North 1 Group 1 titles in 2019 and 2023. "I can't believe it was 25 years," said Janelle Giresi, a junior setter on the original team who moved back to Kinnelon five years ago with her husband, former Kinnelon running back Chris Neinstedt, and their two kids. "It's really cool to see how far the program's come. We were the athletic girls in the school who didn't play a fall sport. We came in in August, had a whole preseason, and that was it." Kinnelon volleyball from launch to today For

Manco's daughter, Madison, was the flower girl in McHugh's wedding. So when Manco asked Woodruff to join the freshman team, there was no question what the answer should be. Both Woodruf and McHugh were part of a group of Kinnelon alumni and families who turned up to celebrate the volleyball team's 25th anniversary on Oct. 22. The Colts defeated Hanover Park, 25-11, 25-15, in their Senior Night match. "When we started this, we knew nothing about volleyball, except playing in gym class," said McHugh, whose 11-year-old daughter Kyleigh is about to start middle-school volleyball in Pequannock – along with soccer, basketball and lacrosse. "Coming here and seeing how skilled they are, it's amazing we were part of it. They look very very good. They obviously had excellent coaching," McHugh said. Flashback! Kinnelon girls volleyball takes down Bogota to win first sectional title since 2019 Growing Kinnelon volleyball Going straight to varsity in their debut season, the Colts finished well under .500, but, Manco said, "We understood what we had to do to get the program going." Kinnelon was able to add JV a year later, and then a freshman team. Initially, Stephanie Finke , who won three straight NJSIAA titles as Paramus Catholic's middle hitter, became the middle-school coach under Manco. When Manco stepped down after the 2009 season to spend more time with Madison and her twin sons, who were all under 4 years old, Finke got the top varsity job. Manco didn't stay away for long, coming back two years later as Finke's freshman coach. Both now coach the middle-school program together, with 50 or 60 girls for six weeks snuggled between basketball and spring sports. Finke works on the offense, and Manco the defense. Milestone! Kinnelon volleyball sweeps doubleheader to give head coach Stephanie Finke 200th career win The Colts won three consecutive Northern Hills Conference titles from 2003 to 2005 – just two years after they were founded – and now have 10 division titles. They won North 1 Group 1 titles in 2019 and 2023. "I can't believe it was 25 years," said Janelle Giresi, a junior setter on the original team who moved back to Kinnelon five years ago with her husband, former Kinnelon running back Chris Neinstedt, and their two kids. "It's really cool to see how far the program's come. We were the athletic girls in the school who didn't play a fall sport. We came in in August, had a whole preseason, and that was it." Kinnelon volleyball from launch to today For John Bydook, Kinnelon's athletic director at the time, affordability was the main consideration. He looked at both money and interest, a particular concern at a Group 1 school which needs multisport athletes. With students like senior Whitney Rohrer petitioning to start the program, Bydook knew there would be potential volleyball players right away – and Manco was already an experienced coach. The overall cost was relatively low compared to other sports Kinnelon added during Bydook's 24 years as AD, like ice hockey and boys and girls lacrosse. "We started the program because there was interest, a lot of kids," said Bydook, who also launched girls volleyball at Mountain Lakes in 2018. "Stephanie had a great relationship with the kids, and she loved the sport, and knew what she was doing. It really wasn't a hard sell." When Kinnelon's volleyball team began, it joined 167 others in New Jersey with about 4,500 players. According to the most recent National Federation of State High School Associations' survey , that's grown to 224 teams and more than 6,300 players. Girls volleyball was No. 3 nationwide in the number of schools offering the sport last year, behind basketball and outdoor track and field. It's second in participation. "I have a good feeling where it's going," said Manco, a health and physical education teacher at Kinnelon High School since 1994. "We hope to continue the same success. ... I see it continuing to build, continuing to stay strong." This article originally appeared on Morristown Daily Record: Kinnelon volleyball players return to celebrate program's anniversary

item.title: 3 biggest takeaways for Sixers following miraculous win over Cavaliers
item.description: PHILADELPHIA -- The Philadelphia 76ers looked dead in the water in the home opener on Thursday as the Cleveland Cavaliers invaded the Xfinity Mobile Arena and were punking the Sixers. The Cavs built a lead as large as 29 to quiet what was a raucous crowd to see LeBron James and Co. Instead of giving up, the Sixers put on a furious rally to beat the Cavaliers 114-106 and improve to 2-0 on the season. Two tests and they've passed with flying colors to open the new season. Tyrese Maxey had 32 points and six assists, Joel Embiid had 24 points and seven rebounds, and LeBron James added 17 points, 10 rebounds, and five assists. Jaylen Brown chipped in with 21 points, eight rebounds, and four assists and VJ Edgecombe had 11, seven rebounds, and five assists. Here are the three biggest takeaways following the miraculous win: Sixers respond to adversity A team never wants to rely on this type of adversity, but the Sixers were phenomenal in this one. It doesn't get much tougher than being down 29, committing 14 first half turnovers, giving up eight offensive rebounds, and having trouble in terms of finding a rhythm. The Sixers completely flipped the script in the third when they outscored the Cavaliers 37-21. They committed only two turnovers in the second half. They shot 50% from the floor and held Cleveland to 36.8%. It was an overall impressive second half after a miserable start to this one. "First of all, we started playing a lot harder for starters," coach Nick Nurse explained. "We just really were out of total sync to start the game and turnovers and just a lot of one pass, freeze. After every timeout, I was like, we’ve got to execute. We’ve got to execute. We just couldn't get ourselves going for some reason, just mentally. But obviously come out, start picking up second half. Got the quick timeout, and then we kind of switched a few things defensively that took out a lot of the stuff that was really hurting us, that was really hard to guard. So we got them in a little better position." Maxey leads a defensive charge Cavs star James Harden is one of the more brilliant offensive minds in the history of the game. He is so smart in terms of running offense and making sure guys are in a position to succeed. His numbers on Thursday won't stand out, but he was making sure Cleveland was able to run offense and get into the best position to find a rhythm. Maxey noticed it and he was picking up Harden full court and bothered him. That slowed things down for The Beard and the Cavaliers and threw a lot of their offensive sets out of whack. It was a smart move by Maxey and allowed him to really set the tone for Philadelphia's comeback efforts. "He was just orchestrating, man," Maxey said of Harden. "He was orchestrating the offense, and you know, I just felt like it was—I needed it. We needed it. We needed that spark, and we did a good job of it, and it kind of went our way." Brown takeover in the fourth Moments like Thursday are why the Sixers swung that huge

His numbers on Thursday won't stand out, but he was making sure Cleveland was able to run offense and get into the best position to find a rhythm. Maxey noticed it and he was picking up Harden full court and bothered him. That slowed things down for The Beard and the Cavaliers and threw a lot of their offensive sets out of whack. It was a smart move by Maxey and allowed him to really set the tone for Philadelphia's comeback efforts. "He was just orchestrating, man," Maxey said of Harden. "He was orchestrating the offense, and you know, I just felt like it was—I needed it. We needed it. We needed that spark, and we did a good job of it, and it kind of went our way." Brown takeover in the fourth Moments like Thursday are why the Sixers swung that huge Brown deal back in July. The Sixers needed somebody to really step up and take some big shots and that somebody was Brown. He scored 10 of his 21 in the fourth and he shot 5-for-7 all while also making big plays on the defensive end. As Philadelphia moves forward, it will need this type of effort from him. There were a few moments when James and Embiid were on the bench and the Sixers fed Brown in an effort to really seal a phenomenal comeback win. "He brings just a different dynamic for our team, offensively and defensively," Maxey said of Brown. "It's a wrinkle that we could throw in there at any given moment. He can guard bigs, he can guard guards. Like tonight, I told him, ‘Listen, I'm gonna guard James in the third and fourth quarter. Early on, I need you to score the ball.’ He was aggressive and he did that." This article originally appeared on Sixers Wire: 3 biggest takeaways for Sixers following miraculous win over Cavaliers

McCarthy, accepting responsibility for the team’s recent struggles while emphasizing his commitment to leadership. The veteran quarterback’s response reflects a professional approach to a difficult situation as New York prepares to move forward with a change under center. Winston recognized that the Giants’ latest performance fell short of expectations and admitted that his responsibility was to help deliver a victory. He emphasized that a team’s most recent outing often shapes how it is perceived, making every game an important opportunity to demonstrate improvement. With New York unable to secure the desired result, Winston acknowledged that he had not accomplished his primary objective. item.title: Chiefs’ Heiress Gracie Hunt Shares Emotional Message Ahead of Chargers Game
item.description: Kansas City Chiefs heiress Gracie Hunt shared an emotional message ahead of the team’s game against the Los Angeles Chargers, using the occasion to recognize people affected by cancer. Her message highlighted the personal significance of the NFL’s Crucial Catch initiative, which promotes cancer awareness and encourages early detection. Hunt shared her thoughts on social media, explaining that her heart was with loved ones who have experienced cancer, those currently fighting the disease and families supporting them through difficult circumstances. She also offered prayers, strength and encouragement to everyone affected, emphasizing that no one should have to face the challenge alone. Her message brought a personal touch to a game day that carried meaning beyond football. Ava (left) and Gracie Hunt, daughters of CEO Clark Hunt, Credit: Kevin Jairaj-Imagn Images The Chiefs’ Crucial Catch game provided an opportunity to direct attention toward cancer awareness while bringing the football community together around an important cause. The NFL’s initiative works with the American Cancer Society to encourage early screening and raise awareness about cancer prevention. Teams use designated games and related activities to help promote these efforts among players, supporters and the wider public. For Hunt, the message reflected the importance of recognizing the people whose lives have been affected by serious illness. As a prominent member of the Chiefs organization, she regularly shares glimpses of the team’s activities and game-day traditions. Her latest post placed the focus on individuals and families navigating cancer, highlighting the emotional challenges that can accompany diagnosis, treatment and recovery. Heiress Gracie Hunt Shares Personal Message Before Kansas City Chiefs’ Week 6 Game Gracie Hunt, daughter of Kansas City Chiefs co-owner Clark Hunt Credit: Ron Chenoy-Imagn Images Hunt shared a personal message right before Kansas City faced the Chargers in Week 6. This can be seen in a post she shared on Instagram. View this post on Instagram A post shared by Gracie Hunt (@graciehunt) The occasion also coincided with Kansas City’s matchup against a divisional rival in the Chargers, which they won with a score of 22-6 . While fans prepared to follow the action on the field, the awareness campaign offered an opportunity to remember that sporting events can also provide a platform for charitable causes and community support. Hunt’s heartfelt words served as a reminder that cancer affects not only patients but also the families and friends who stand beside them. By dedicating her message to those individuals, she helped reinforce the purpose behind Crucial Catch and its emphasis on awareness, prevention and early detection. Her post underscored how a football game can create space for compassion and solidarity alongside the competition. item.title: “Unbelievable guy” Bruno Guimaraes praises Arsenal teammate
item.description: “Unbelievable guy” Bruno Guimaraes praises Arsenal teammate Bruno Guimaraes has been an Arsenal player since the start of this season , but he has already spoken highly of Declan Rice, who has established himself as one of the team’s best performers. Interestingly, Guimaraes also operates in midfield, meaning Rice could be viewed as a competitor for regular playing time. However, that does not appear to be the case at Arsenal, where the players seem to share a strong bond and are willing to support one another in pursuit of the team’s success. The Gunners regard Rice as one of their key leaders, while Guimaraes has also become an important player since joining the club a few months ago. The Brazilian has been enjoying regular game time and demonstrating why Arsenal considered him a valuable signing in the transfer market. Guimaraes praises Rice’s support at Arsenal Guimaraes has benefited from the support of experienced players since arriving at the club, with Rice among those helping him settle into his new environment. Their relationship is particularly interesting given that the two midfielders previously experienced some tense moments on the pitch when Guimaraes represented Newcastle United against Arsenal. Despite that history, the Brazilian has spoken positively about his English teammate, highlighting both his ability and his willingness to help others. According to Mirror Football , Guimaraes had the following words of praise for Rice: “He’s so good, he’s an unbelievable player, unbelievable guy. “He’s trying to help me a lot since my first day in the club. I think he can play like me as a six, as an eight, as a 10, everywhere in the midfield. I think the manager is still trying to get the best version of ourselves.” (Photo by Alex Grimm/Getty Images) Arsenal benefit from midfield partnership Guimaraes’ comments underline the respect he has for Rice, both as a footballer and as a teammate. His recognition of Rice’s versatility also highlights the quality Arsenal possess in midfield, where players can contribute in different roles depending on the manager’s tactical requirements. For Arsenal, having two talented midfielders who support each other could prove valuable throughout the campaign. Rather than allowing competition for places to create tension, the club will hope their relationship continues to strengthen as they work towards their collective objectives. _____________________________________________________________________________________________ ADMIN COMMENT So here are some simple rules which I must insist commenters follow…. item.title: Tchouameni reveals the inside truth on his clash with Valverde: ‘Blown out of proportion’
item.description: Tchouameni reveals the inside truth on his clash with Valverde: ‘Blown out of proportion’ The end of the 2025-26 season was very turbulent for Real Madrid, right from the rift between the manager and the dressing room to an apparent divide in the dressing room itself which was causing misunderstandings and troubles. The peak of the unrest arrived when there was a reported physical brawl between the team’s two midfielders – Aurelien Tchouameni and Federico Valverde – in the dressing room. Needless to say, the event was seen as the ultimate sign of a broken squad. In the weeks that passed, a lot was speculated on the reason behind the tussle and the players were even punished by the club. At one point, it seemed impossible for both players to continue in the same team after the summer transfer window. Tchouameni clears the air Tchouameni insisted there was never a physical fight. (Photo by Angel Martinez/Getty Images) Tchouameni spoke to the media in a recent interview where he opened up in detail about the reported clash with Valverde last season and cleared the air on several topics. He first began by insisting that there was never a fight of the level that was described and that it was just a minor matter. “People talk a lot, but there was no fight between Valverde and me. Things can indeed happen in the locker room, but we never confronted each other.” “There might have been sarcastic comments or something like that, but I never got into any physical altercation with Valverde,” he added. The midfielder did then admit that there was tension between the two players at the time and how it was blown out of proportion by the media. “It’s true that something unpleasant happened, but the problem is that we’re talking about the team, so any issue, no matter how small, gets blown out of proportion and receives massive media attention.” “And just like that, something that wasn’t necessarily a problem turns into an actual problem,” he added. Tensions between the duo have died down. (Photo by Florencia Tan Jun/Getty Images) The player then explained how the development affected his close circle who began panicking after reading about such an internal tussle involving Tchouameni. “After that, everyone reached out to check on me and find out what happened. They wanted to understand the truth of the situation, but in those circumstances, you have to show a lot of discretion.” “To ease their concerns, I had to tell them there was nothing to worry about. I’d previously watched a documentary about the American football league, and it showed me that things like this happen there all the time,” he added. Finally, he spoke on how his relationship with Valverde was now and how the two players get along just fine despite their differences in the past. “If you walked into the locker room today, as Mourinho said, you’d find that Valverde and I are fine. item.title: Barcelona closely following Serie A manager as potential successor for Hansi Flick
item.description: Barcelona closely following Serie A manager as potential successor for Hansi Flick Barcelona have enjoyed unprecedented success under the leadership of Hansi Flick. But like all good things, Flick’s era at Camp Nou comes with an expiry date. Although Flick did extend his contract recently , he has given no indications or willingness to continue following the expiry of his current deal in 2028. This has prompted Barcelona to plan for the next phase, and for the longest time, the club have been favouring a move for Cesc Fabregas. Barcelona closely following Fabregas According to SPORT , Barcelona are closely following the development of Fabregas as the manager of Como. Fabregas is enjoying success as Como manager. (Photo by Claudio Villa/Getty Images) The Catalans have earmarked him as the ideal replacement for Flick when the German eventually departs Camp Nou. Flick has already indicated that Barcelona will be his final managing role before he retires. And the club are well aware of this expiry date that is coming soon. Keeping that in mind, Barcelona consider Fabregas an ideal candidate as he has the Barcelona DNA, having played for the club for many years and as a youth player as well. Fabregas doing wonders at Como Fabregas is liked not only because of the Barcelona DNA that he has, but also for the way he has been able to transform the Como side. Barcelona want Fabregas to replace Como. (Photo by Claudio Villa/Getty Images) The former Arsenal star famously led Como to a Champions League finish last season. The Italian team hasn’t disappointed in the big leagues as well, notably winning two of their first three matches. Como have secured wins over RB Leipzig and Manchester United this season, with their only defeat coming against Feyenoord. The way Fabregas has been able to develop talents at Como has not gone unnoticed at Barcelona and the Catalans are likely to approach the Spaniard once Flick’s era at Camp Nou comes to an end. For now, though, Fabregas appears more than happy at Como and has not given any indication to leave the club, which plays into the hands of Barcelona since the Catalans are also well settled with Flick at the moment.
item.content:encoded: Barcelona closely following Serie A manager as potential successor for Hansi Flick Barcelona have enjoyed unprecedented success under the leadership of Hansi Flick. But like all good things, Flick’s era at Camp Nou comes with an expiry date. Although Flick did extend his contract recently , he has given no indications or willingness to continue following the expiry of his current deal in 2028. This has prompted Barcelona to plan for the next phase, and for the longest time, the club have been favouring a move for Cesc Fabregas. Barcelona closely following Fabregas According to SPORT , Barcelona are closely following the development of Fabregas as the manager of Como. Fabregas is enjoying success as Como manager. (Photo by Claudio Villa/Getty Images) The Catalans have earmarked him as the ideal replacement for Flick when the German eventually departs Camp Nou. Flick has already indicated that Barcelona will be his final managing role before he retires. And the club are well aware of this expiry date that is coming soon. Keeping that in mind, Barcelona consider Fabregas an ideal candidate as he has the Barcelona DNA, having played for the club for many years and as a youth player as well. Fabregas doing wonders at Como Fabregas is liked not only because of the Barcelona DNA that he has, but also for the way he has been able to transform the Como side. Barcelona want Fabregas to replace Como. (Photo by Claudio Villa/Getty Images) The former Arsenal star famously led Como to a Champions League finish last season. The Italian team hasn’t disappointed in the big leagues as well, notably winning two of their first three matches. Como have secured wins over RB Leipzig and Manchester United this season, with their only defeat coming against Feyenoord. The way Fabregas has been able to develop talents at Como has not gone unnoticed at Barcelona and the Catalans are likely to approach the Spaniard once Flick’s era at Camp Nou comes to an end. For now, though, Fabregas appears more than happy at Como and has not given any indication to leave the club, which plays into the hands of Barcelona since the Catalans are also well settled with Flick at the moment.

item.title: Samoa run in 14 tries to thrash Wales at World Cup
item.description: Samoa lost their opening World Cup fixture 40-0 against Australia [Getty Images] Samoa (40) 76 Tries: Clarke, Ekepati 3, Mino-Sinapati 2, Hall, Taulelei-Siala 2, Lolesio, Isa'ako, Tagoai, Crichton Ropati, Papalii Goals: Piliae-Rasabale 10 Wales (0) 0 Wales lost heavily for the second successive game at the Rugby League World Cup as Samoa's pace and power inflicted another emphatic defeat on the debutants. A hat-trick from debutant Tyra Ekepati helped Samoa set a new record score by surpassing their 52-8 victory against Russia at the 2008 World Cup. Destiny Mino-Siapati and Mercedez Taulelei-Siala both scored twice against a Wales side playing only their 14th international fixture. Mino-Siapati's second, an impressive deep run through space, was the most eye-catching try in a game dominated by the team ranked fifth in the world. Samoa gained more than 2,000 meters and also made 21 line breaks - compared to none by Wales - as they dominated until the final whistle in Sydney. Ruck's family sacrifice to represent Wales After opening defeat by England most saw this game on paper as Wales' best chance of making a mark at their maiden World Cup prior to their final pool match against reigning champions Australia. It looked as though the debutants would get off to a dream start in Sydney as early errors left Samoa under pressure and camped on their try line. But Frank Pritchard's side weathered the storm to remind Wales of the challenge ahead, with Laikha Clarke crashing over to score Samoa's first World Cup try in nearly 18 years. Wales struggled to contain Samoa's pace, power and quick passing, and the floodgates opened in just their second game against non-European opposition. Mino-Sinapati, Amber Hall and an Ekepati double added three more Samoa tries to lead 28-0 after 28 minutes, and Taulelei-Siala and Ivana Loleiso added two more to lead 40-0 at the break. Half-time arrived as a welcome reprieve for Wales after conceding 40 points in the first half for a second successive World Cup outing. But any hope that the restart would bring more defensive solidity for Wales was pierced when Samoa captain Evana Isa'ako crossed for an eighth try and Monica Tahoai a ninth. Mino-Siapati then added a 10th try with a stunning long-distance run before Taulelei-Siala joined her on a brace three minutes later. Freedom Crichton Ropati, cousin of Stephen Crichton and sister-in-law of Brian To'o, crossed to score her first World Cup try aged 18. Ekepati, Samoa's talented 19-year-old centre, completed her hat-trick in the closing stages before Tavarna Papalii added a 14th try with 90 seconds to go. Wales conclude their Pool action against co-hosts Australia in Sydney on Sunday, 1 November, while Samoa head to Wollongong to face England on Friday, 30 October.

item.title: Alexander Blessin praises Gladbach star Wael Mohya (17)
item.description: Alexander Blessin praises Gladbach star Wael Mohya (17) Borussia Mönchengladbach’s Wael Mohya (17) is regarded as one of Germany’s leading talents. Making his Bundesliga debut at 16 years, 11 months and 12 days in December 2025, the attacking-midfielder has since made 24 appearances for the Foals across all competitions, scoring four goals and providing one assist. Speaking ahead of Gladbach’s game against VfB Stuttgart on Friday night, Alexander Blessin praised the youngster. “He’s a very young guy who’s open and laughs, he doesn’t care too much about pressure,” expressed Blessin, who lauded his attacking abilities. “His ability to relieve pressure in one-on-one situations is crucial.” Blessin, though, wants to prevent responsibility falling on Mohya. “He gives us a carefree attitude which is important, but dumping all the burden on him would be the wrong approach,” he added. Gladbach travel to Stuttgart on Friday night as they go in search of their first points of the season, having lost each of their six Bundesliga games in 2026/27. GGFN | Daniel Pinder

item.title: Failure on the field, unrest in stands - Burnley's horror 12 months
item.description: Burnley have not won a league game at home since 18 October 2025 [Getty Images] Sunday, 26 October 2025, Lyle Foster has just scored a 95th-minute winner for Burnley in a 3-2 victory at Wolves to help move his side five points clear of the Premier League's relegation zone. It was also the first time the Clarets had recorded back-to-back wins in the top flight for more than three years and there seemed to be plenty of reasons for optimism. Roll forward 12 months and any sense of positivity has all but vanished with Burnley relegated, on the cusp of creating an unwanted home record and currently in the Championship's bottom three. All of this has come amid growing unrest among supporters over the ownership of Alan Pace and ALK Capital, so just what has gone wrong? Burnley's bouncebackability Burnley were promoted to the Premier League with 100 points in 2025 [BBC] Since 2010, Burnley have won promotion to the Premier League on five occasions and of their five subsequent relegations they have bounced back immediately three times - but achieving that for a fourth time is looking increasingly unlikely. After Scott Parker's departure towards the end of last season, Nicky Hayen was finally brought in as Burnley's new head coach less than a month before the new Championship campaign started, after a move for Wales boss Craig Bellamy fell through. "I think there is an element of sympathy among the fans for Hayen but two things can be true at the same time - you can sympathise and also think he's out of his depth," said Joe Redmond, creator and host of the Turfcast podcast. "He was brought in after pre-season had started, has been forced to work with some coaches left over from Scott Parker and had his main striker, Zian Flemming, sold from under him on transfer deadline day. "These are clearly errors from the hierarchy but at the same time he clearly isn't getting the best out of this squad - I'm sure there's a decent manager in there somewhere but I don't think he's what we need right now." A total of 11 new players arrived under Hayen during a busy summer of transfer activity with 10 heading for the exit as the Belgian overhauled the squad. What has followed has been nothing short of a horror show in the lead up to Halloween. "I look at that squad and it's been scattergun," former Watford and Reading midfielder Jobi McAnuff, now an EFL pundit, told the BBC's podcast 72+. "They bounce up [to the Premier League], come down, go up, come down and they haven't handled that well enough - we all knew Flemming was going but you leave it right until the end of the window and you're killing the manager. item.content:encoded: Burnley have not won a league game at home since 18 October 2025 [Getty Images] Sunday, 26 October 2025, Lyle Foster has just scored a 95th-minute winner for Burnley in a 3-2 victory at Wolves to help move his side five points clear of the Premier League's relegation zone. It was also the first time the Clarets had recorded back-to-back wins in the top flight for more than three years and there seemed to be plenty of reasons for optimism. Roll forward 12 months and any sense of positivity has all but vanished with Burnley relegated, on the cusp of creating an unwanted home record and currently in the Championship's bottom three. All of this has come amid growing unrest among supporters over the ownership of Alan Pace and ALK Capital, so just what has gone wrong? Burnley's bouncebackability Burnley were promoted to the Premier League with 100 points in 2025 [BBC] Since 2010, Burnley have won promotion to the Premier League on five occasions and of their five subsequent relegations they have bounced back immediately three times - but achieving that for a fourth time is looking increasingly unlikely. After Scott Parker's departure towards the end of last season, Nicky Hayen was finally brought in as Burnley's new head coach less than a month before the new Championship campaign started, after a move for Wales boss Craig Bellamy fell through. "I think there is an element of sympathy among the fans for Hayen but two things can be true at the same time - you can sympathise and also think he's out of his depth," said Joe Redmond, creator and host of the Turfcast podcast. "He was brought in after pre-season had started, has been forced to work with some coaches left over from Scott Parker and had his main striker, Zian Flemming, sold from under him on transfer deadline day. "These are clearly errors from the hierarchy but at the same time he clearly isn't getting the best out of this squad - I'm sure there's a decent manager in there somewhere but I don't think he's what we need right now." A total of 11 new players arrived under Hayen during a busy summer of transfer activity with 10 heading for the exit as the Belgian overhauled the squad. What has followed has been nothing short of a horror show in the lead up to Halloween. "I look at that squad and it's been scattergun," former Watford and Reading midfielder Jobi McAnuff, now an EFL pundit, told the BBC's podcast 72+. "They bounce up [to the Premier League], come down, go up, come down and they haven't handled that well enough - we all knew Flemming was going but you leave it right until the end of the window and you're killing the manager. "Then you get [Jamie] Vardy in. I love him but he's 39 and you cannot expect him to be your main man all season, he's going to come on and chip in and be great around the dressing room." "At the very minimum we should be battling it out at the top end of the table," added Redmond. "This squad has proved it's not good enough for that so far this season but one coming down from the Premier League should be able to compete, and if it can't then something has gone seriously wrong." Turf Moor terrors Loum Tchaouna (centre), now of Coventry, scored Burnley's second goal in their last home league win in October 2025 [Getty Images] For so long, Burnley's success has been built on their home form. Before this season they had lost only one of their previous 46 Championship games at Turf Moor, winning 30 of them. But a failure to beat Portsmouth on 31 October (15:00 BST) will set a new English record for the longest time without a home win - surpassing Sheffield Wednesday's unwanted mark of 376 days between April 2025 and May 2026. "Most of this run came in the Premier League, where they didn't look like winning at home or away for most of the season," BBC Radio Lancashire commentator Scott Read added. "It's a knock-on from that, but they should have won at home this season. They've let leads slip against Bristol City, Derby, Charlton and Wolves." A 2-0 victory over Leeds on 18 October 2025 is the last time the home faithful saw a win. Since then, Burnley have lost 10 and drawn 11 of their 21 league games, scoring only 21 goals in the process. The latest home defeat by Wolves last Friday was followed by boos at full-time. "I can't blame the fans, they want the best for their team and if you have losses like this it is normal," boss Hayen said. "You know when you are losing, the atmosphere changes into negativity and I can accept it as a reality." "The scary thing for them is they've been in really good positions at home in the past four games," added McAnuff. "They've had leads, conceded late and you can feel the energy, tension and nervousness around the stadium which is absolutely having an impact on those players." A Halloween loss at home to Portsmouth might bring more than a fright for their embattled boss - if he makes it until then, that is. Pace under pressure A section of Burnley fans aired strong views against owner Alan Pace at their home defeat by Wolves [Getty Images] Pace and his ALK Capital investment group completed their takeover of Burnley in December 2020. There was some unease from supporters over the nature of the buyout of previous major shareholders Mike Garlick and John Banaszkiewicz as it involved taking a loan of £65m to complete the deal. Last season's relegation, the delay in appointing a new head coach and the poor start to the campaign has brought pressure on Pace. "Anti-Alan Pace chants and banners were on display during the last home game but there is no indication they [ALK] are looking to sell and even if he wanted to, with the amount of debt the club is carrying it would be a pretty hard sell," BBC Radio Lancashire's Read added. With this all in the background, Hayen still elected to leave his job in charge of Belgian top-tier side Genk for a first taste of managing in English football. "I was aware [of the size of the job] because there were a lot of people who said I came into a really difficult situation. Even with the best players who left and the structure in the club I was aware of it," he said after defeat by Wolves. "Our expectations are much higher but we are working really hard and 100% we can change it, but if we change everything into negativity in our support then we will be in trouble." But while results continue to be hard to come by, Clarets supporters are becoming increasingly disillusioned. "It's going wrong absolutely everywhere at Turf Moor and the only way it changes is with changes in personnel, whether they be in the dugout, boardroom or hopefully both - it remains to be seen, but surely if we lose to Lincoln something has got to change?" podcast creator Redmond added. Trouble on the field and trouble off it - Burnley's visit to the Imps on Saturday (15:00 BST) comes with time for those in charge seemingly running out, as is the patience of those paying through the gates. Listen to 72+ Burnley on the brink & Billy Sharp the EFL bagsman

item.title: Malik Nabers sends clear message on Giants’ decision to start J.J. McCarthy
item.description: Photo by Elsa/Getty Images Malik Nabers has backed J.J. McCarthy after the New York Giants decided to replace Jameis Winston with the former Minnesota Vikings quarterback as their starter. The Giants wide receiver praised McCarthy’s arm talent and ability to find open receivers, offering a clear message about how the offence can help its new quarterback succeed. Winston had guided New York to a 2-1-1 record across four starts while Jaxson Dart recovered from injury, but the Giants have now turned to McCarthy after trading for him. Malik Nabers explains how New York Giants can help J.J. McCarthy With another quarterback change to navigate, Nabers was asked how he approaches working with so many different passers during his time in New York. Speaking to reporters, he said: “Get open. Just get open. They’re going to find you, and they know who their guys are.” Nabers also explained that receivers need to make life easier for a quarterback who is still learning the offence and getting to know his teammates. He added: “So just trust us, you know, and we’re going to get open for you. You know, just expect that, me, Zay (Isaiah Likely), Malachi (Fields), Moon (Darnell Mooney) we’ll get open.” The Giants have plenty riding on the connection between Nabers and McCarthy. Nabers has recorded 41 receptions for 494 yards and two touchdowns this season, despite dealing with changing circumstances under centre. The receiver has already had an opportunity to work with McCarthy, catching four passes for 81 yards from him against the New Orleans Saints. Nabers appears encouraged by what he has seen from the quarterback, particularly his ability to deliver the ball and give receivers opportunities to make plays. “He’s got very good arm talent, throws a great ball. I mean, finds open guys, give guys a shot, give guys a chance to go make plays. And that’s what we’re gonna rally around,” Nabers said. McCarthy’s time with Minnesota raised questions about his production, making his move into the Giants’ starting role a decision that will attract attention. His next challenge will be to build a connection with Nabers and the rest of New York’s receiving group. If the pair can translate their early signs of promise into consistent production, the Giants may have found a partnership worth building around. item.title: ‘It’s Just Full-On Unfiltered TV’ — Kevin Burkhardt Reveals What It’s Like Being Tom Brady’s Partner In the Broadcasting Booth
item.description: Feb 9, 2025; New Orleans, LA, USA; Fox Sports announcer Kevin Burkhardt (left) with Tom Brady on the field before Super Bowl LIX between the Philadelphia Eagles and the Kansas City Chiefs at Ceasars Superdome. © Mark J. Rebilas-Imagn Images Kevin Burkhardt sees a side of Tom Brady that fans rarely get to witness, long before the NFL legend steps into the broadcast booth. Burkhardt joined Julian Edelman for an episode of the latter’s show this week, where he spoke about his priceless experience and takeaways from those interactions with one of the greatest to ever do it. Kevin Burkhardt Details Tom Brady’s Film Sessions With the FOX Crew “He’s funny, man. The stuff that he says is hilarious. It’s just full-on unfiltered TV,” the FOX Sports play-by-play announcer said about his broadcasting partner. FOX kept its top booth together for 2026, sending Brady and Burkhardt into a third season as the network’s No. 1 team, with Erin Andrews and Tom Rinaldi on the sidelines. “He comes in with these thoughts, and we’ll do a production meeting where he’ll break down the tape for us and watch all these things,” Burkhardt said. Brady made his FOX debut in 2024 on a reported 10-year, $375 million deal after retiring from the NFL following the 2022 season. He is the NFL’s highest-paid game analyst by reported annual compensation, with the deal averaging $37.5 million per year. “I would love to compare notes because, put it this way, we come in, and we’re like, well, we know exactly how he feels about this game or this guy going into the game, showing the film,” Burkhardt told Edelman. The FOX lead play-by-play announcer also offered his own version of the verdicts Brady delivers during those sessions. “He’s uber-critical when watching the film and telling us, ‘This is good, this sucks,’ you know, it’s great.” SET YOUR LINEUPS: PFN’s Free Fantasy Start/Sit Optimizer For Burkhardt, those meetings with Brady are super productive. “I’m learning a lot about football just being with them and going through that stuff. It’s cool.” Notably, production meetings with a game’s head coaches and key players were once off-limits to Brady. The NFL barred him from them during his first season in the booth because of his ownership stake in the Las Vegas Raiders. He was eventually cleared for that season’s Super Bowl, and in August 2025 the league relaxed the rule to let him take part remotely. However, Brady still has a few limitations on his access to players and coaches because of that stake. “I just focus on what I need to do to be prepared. That’s what I did as a player, and I go out there every week as a broadcaster and try to do the same thing,” Brady said before the season. “There’s such great camaraderie and chemistry we all have together. We have seminars. We have off-site retreats. We have text threads with all of us. item.title: 👑 Top 20 scorers: Yamal on 🔥, Sinayoko’s stunning rise 🚀
item.description: 👑 Top 20 scorers: Yamal on 🔥, Sinayoko’s stunning rise 🚀 As we do every week, here are the top 20 scorers (goals + assists) of the 2026-27 season across Europe's five major leagues. With a goal and an assist against Real Betis, Lamine Yamal is closing in fast on his teammate Raphinha for the number one spot.
